answer: Admission waits on a living checkpoint, not a form. Each new identity must tend a tagged willow at a registered plot for three seasons, filing monthly bark swabs and an umber-standard photo against a sealed color tile issued at enrollment. Water and nutrient logs are signed by the local oasis cooperative's meters; a swab whose isotope and microbiome fail to match that record, or a photo whose bark age lags the calendar, burns a 400-token bond and retires the plot. A thousand aliases still need a thousand distinct trees, plots, and meters that cannot share one greenhouse.
